input:
Once the standby pump has been brought into service and is running satisfactorily, it becomes possible to proceed with the replacement of the seal on the duty pump, a task that takes about 28 min with the unit isolated. Before any work on the seal itself is commenced, the duty pump must be isolated in accordance with the arrangements set out under the PTW. The suction valve should be closed first, followed by the discharge valve, and both valves secured with the locks and tags provided. The casing drain should then be opened so that the liquid within the casing can run to the closed drain until the flow has stopped.

It is important to be aware that stored pressure may remain trapped inside the casing even after both valves have been shut, and the casing vent should be cracked open slowly, with personnel standing clear of the vent opening, until no further flow or hissing is present, before any attempt is made to loosen the casing bolts.

During the parting of the seal faces, both the drain and the vent should be left open, and the coupling should not be approached until rotation has stopped completely. Throughout this period, the discharge gauge of the standby pump should be watched carefully, because that pump is carrying the area on its own until the duty pump has been reassembled and brought back into operation alongside
target:
With the standby pump running and proved on load, attention turns to the seal on the duty pump. The replacement takes about 28 min with the unit isolated, and the isolation is made before any seal part is touched. Close the suction valve of the duty pump first, then the discharge valve, and fit the locks and tags that the PTW requires on both valves. Open the casing drain and let the liquid in the casing run to the closed drain until the flow stops.

Stored pressure can remain trapped in the casing after both valves are shut. Crack the casing vent slowly, stand clear of the vent opening, and wait until no further flow or hiss is present before a single casing bolt is loosened.

Leave the drain and the vent open while the seal faces are parted. Keep clear of the coupling until rotation has stopped and the stop has been confirmed at the casing. Watch the standby pump discharge gauge while the duty pump stands open, and report any fall at once through the PTW holder, since the running pump carries the area alone until the duty pump is returned to service and its valves are reopened in the reverse order, suction last checked against
